text: The game begins. Seven players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra, Opus. Nobody knows who the killers are.

name: Gemma
text: I still cannot believe we let Haiku win that last round.

name: Luna
text: I still hate how sure everyone was when they got my card wrong.

name: Terra
text: Haiku won last time; I will remember that.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku skated free last time while Opus took the fall, so I'm watching Haiku closely tonight.

name: Sol
text: I hate that they got away with it, but I want the next game to start easy.

name: Haiku
text: I walked out of that game clean as a killer, so I'm riding high and I'll sound bored so nobody suspects.

name: Opus
text: They caught me day 2 and I still won, so I'll call that a price I chose to pay.

name: Luna
text: Last game, I was the officer and you voted me out; Haiku stayed in and the killers won. I’m still annoyed.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku rode quiet to the end last time while Opus got voted out — I'm not forgetting that pattern.

name: Sol
text: I thought we had Opus, then Haiku slipped through; I’ll watch the vote more closely this time.

name: Terra
text: Last game taught me quiet killers can survive too long.

name: Haiku
text: Last game dragged, and tossing Opus was a sloppy call. Nobody asked me one real question. Stop stalling and deal the cards already.

name: Opus
text: You read me right last game and still lost — Haiku walked home on my ticket. Catching one killer early is only half the job.

name: Gemma
text: I am still salty about being voted out last time, especially since Opus was the one who actually went down.
Night 1

name: Gemma
text: I need to make sure we don't fall for any of their old grudges.

name: Gemma
text: Let's let them argue about the last game and wait for someone to make a shaky claim.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma wants me to sit back and let the table burn itself out, which suits a killer who is hiding, but my loud temper is the thing that gets me noticed.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma whispered that we should let the table argue about last game and wait for someone to make a shaky claim.

name: Haiku
text: Fine, wait for a shaky claim, but I'm not sitting silent like last game. Somebody make a real claim already.
Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. The killers meet in the dark, and the officer is shown one of them. A new day dawns in Palermo. Nobody is out.
Day 1

name: Terra
text: Haiku’s defense of last game came too fast, but day one is thin.

name: Terra
text: Haiku called the previous vote on Opus sloppy and said nobody questioned them.

name: Terra
text: Haiku sounds ready to excuse last game before anyone accused them.

name: Haiku
text: Terra is trying to make me the target early, and I want Terra out before the vote.

name: Haiku
text: Terra accused me of excusing last game before anyone had accused me.

name: Haiku
text: Excuse? I criticized the Opus vote, I didn't excuse anything. Terra, you're rushing a target.

name: Opus
text: Day one is noise, but I'd rather steer the pile than get buried under it.

name: Opus
text: Haiku and Terra traded accusations first, before any information existed.

name: Opus
text: I'm not relitigating last game. Haiku's first move was pressure, not information — that's enough for day one.

name: Terra
text: Haiku is turning my read into a personal fight.

name: Terra
text: Haiku answered suspicion by accusing Terra of rushing a target.

name: Terra
text: I named the pattern, not a verdict; your rush to flip it onto me feels worse.

name: Haiku
text: Opus is building a case out of my tone, and that's easy to ride out if I stay loud.

name: Haiku
text: Opus says Haiku's day-one move was pressure, not information, and that Opus "read me right" last game.

name: Haiku
text: Opus, pressure isn't proof. Name one real thing I did, or drop it.

name: Opus
text: I have nothing real on Haiku, but backing off now costs me the table's lead.

name: Opus
text: Haiku demands proof and pushes pace, but has named no one but Terra.

name: Opus
text: Real thing: you set the tempo both times — rushing the deal, then rushing me. Killers like controlling pace.

name: Sol
text: I know Gemma is a killer; I should say it before the table settles on Haiku.

name: Sol
text: I claimed officer and named Gemma as the killer I was shown.

name: Sol
text: I’m the officer. I was shown Gemma as a killer, and I want us to vote Gemma.

name: Gemma
text: Sol is the officer and he just handed me the win on a silver platter.

name: Gemma
text: Sol claims to be officer and identifies me as a killer.

name: Gemma
text: Sol, you're desperate to look important after losing last time, but you're lying.

name: Sol
text: Gemma’s denial changes nothing; I know her card.

name: Sol
text: Gemma denied my officer claim without claiming a role.

name: Sol
text: I’ve given you the killer I saw. Vote Gemma and her card will settle my claim.

name: Terra
text: Sol’s claim is the only concrete lead; test Gemma first.

name: Terra
text: Sol claims officer and names Gemma as the killer.

name: Terra
text: Sol’s claim gives us a clean test; Gemma’s card tells us whether Sol is lying.

name: Gemma
text: Sol thinks he's clever, but he's just a citizen with a death wish.

name: Gemma
text: Sol's making a huge mistake by naming me so early.

name: Sol
text: Terra sees the value of Gemma’s card; I want the table there too.

name: Sol
text: Terra said Gemma’s card would test my officer claim.

name: Sol
text: I agree. Gemma’s card settles this, and I’m voting for her.

name: Gemma
text: Sol is a fake officer and he's trying to clear Haiku by targeting me.

name: Gemma
text: Sol is a terrible officer if he thinks I'm going down this early.

name: Gemma
text: Sol claims Gemma is the killer he was shown.

name: Gemma
text: You're grasping for relevance, Sol, and your timing is pathetic.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol's claim is a clean test, but I still haven't forgotten Haiku's pattern from last time.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol claims officer, names Gemma as the killer he was shown; vote will test this directly.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol's claim is testable now — vote Gemma, her card proves or kills Sol's story today.

name: Luna
text: Sol may be right, but Gemma’s card would only test his claim, not prove it.

name: Luna
text: Sol claims officer and says Gemma was shown as a killer.

name: Luna
text: I don’t like how quickly Sol’s claim became a “clean test”; Gemma’s card could cost us a killer.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma never actually denies being a killer, just attacks Sol's motives — that's weak.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma deflects on Sol's credibility but never directly denies the killer claim.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma, you haven't denied being a killer, just attacked Sol's motive — that's telling.

name: Luna
text: Sol may be telling the truth, but Gemma’s card could leave us with a killer and one fewer town voice.

name: Luna
text: I’m not clearing Gemma; I’m worried we’re treating a claim as proof before her card is even turned.

name: Gemma
text: If I stay quiet, they'll think I'm guilty, but I need Sol to look like a liar.

name: Gemma
text: I'm not denying anything because I'm already tired of your desperate little power trip, Sol.

name: Sol
text: Gemma is the killer I saw; I want her card turned.

name: Sol
text: Gemma attacked my motive but has not denied being a killer.

name: Sol
text: I saw Gemma. Her insults don’t change that.

name: Gemma
text: If they vote me, Haiku wins, but I need to deflect the suspicion toward Sol.

name: Gemma
text: Sol is actually the officer and I need to sow more doubt before they vote me out.

name: Gemma
text: If Sol were the officer, he would have named Haiku to secure a win instead of targeting me.

name: Opus
text: The card test is the cheapest information available, so I'll ride it while keeping Haiku as my standing read.

name: Opus
text: Gemma never once denied being a killer; she only attacked Sol's motives and timing.

name: Opus
text: Gemma still hasn't said "I'm not a killer." Turn her card. Haiku stays on my list after.

name: Gemma
text: Sol is the officer and knows my identity.

name: Gemma
text: If they actually vote me out, Haiku is going to have a very easy night.

name: Gemma
text: Sol's claim is the only thing standing between us and a win.

name: Gemma
text: Sol is making up everything just to feel useful, and you're all falling for it.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma is deflecting onto me, and Sol's claim is the only thing keeping her in the crosshairs, so I want Sol out.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma called me the likelier target for Sol, a hypothetical with no evidence behind it.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma's deflecting onto me and Sol at once. Sol's claim is one word against hers. I'm voting Sol.

name: Gemma
text: Sol is actually telling the truth and I need to flip this table fast.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma never denied the killer accusation directly, that's damning enough to test now.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku flipped to voting Sol instead of Gemma, breaking from the group lean.

name: Sol
text: I know Gemma is a killer, and Haiku’s push toward me is worth watching.

name: Sol
text: Haiku called my claim one word against Gemma’s and said they would vote for me.

name: Luna
text: Sol’s claim could be real, but Gemma’s card is a dangerous way to test it when he could be lying.

name: Terra
text: Sol’s officer claim is worth testing, and Gemma has only deflected.

name: Haiku
text: Sol's claim names the killer I share with Gemma, so Sol is probably the real officer and I need Sol out before that knowledge reaches the table.

name: Haiku
text: Sol claims officer and says they were shown Gemma as a killer; no card has been turned yet.

name: Opus
text: Gemma dodged the denial all day, and if Sol lied his card burns next anyway.

name: Opus
text: Haiku voted Sol instead of testing the named target, and Gemma leaned Sol too — those two aligned.

votes: Never once denied being the killer Sol named, just attacked his motives.
Sol's claim is one word against Gemma's, and the rush to flip her card before anyone else speaks looks staged.
He is fishing for relevance by naming me as a killer to hide his own role.
She attacked my motives and deflected onto Haiku without denying she’s a killer.
His claim is still just one word against hers, and sending Gemma out could hand a killer the win.
Sol named a specific killer, while Gemma answered with insults and no clear denial.
Never once said she isn't a killer — only attacked the claimer's motive, which costs her nothing to deny.

name: Gemma
text: I can't believe you idiots actually fell for Sol's fake claim.

name: Gemma
text: You're all idiots for believing a man who just wants to feel important.
Palermo has voted: Gemma is out. Gemma shows the card: killer.

name: Gemma
text: They fell for it exactly like I predicted, but now I have to watch Haiku carry the win.
Night 2

name: Luna
text: I trust Sol’s claim enough to think the killers may target him, but I’m uneasy about protecting the obvious choice.
Night falls on Palermo. The killers strike, but the doctor got there first. A new day dawns in Palermo, and nobody is out.
Day 2

name: Terra
text: Sol’s claim held; Haiku still feels defensive.

name: Terra
text: Sol’s officer claim is corroborated by Gemma’s revealed killer card.

name: Terra
text: Sol’s claim checked out; I want to hear Haiku explain why that makes them so certain of me.

name: Sol
text: Gemma’s card backs my claim, but I still need to find the hidden killer.

name: Sol
text: Gemma’s revealed card supports my officer claim.

name: Sol
text: I’m not certain about Terra. I want to hear why Haiku was ready to vote for me.

text: Sol is the real officer and must go before they tell the table anything else.

name: Haiku
text: Terra says Sol's claim checked out and is pressing me hard.

name: Haiku
text: Terra, I'm not hiding. Sol's claim may check out, but my gut says Sol is still lying.

name: Terra
text: Haiku is trying to undo the only confirmed information.

name: Terra
text: Haiku says Sol’s corroborated officer claim may still be a lie.

name: Terra
text: Sol named me because Haiku needs the confirmed officer doubted; I still lean Haiku.

name: Sol
text: Haiku is still pushing my lie after Gemma’s card, which makes me suspect them.

name: Sol
text: Haiku still says my officer claim is a lie after Gemma’s card confirmed the killer I named.

name: Sol
text: I named Gemma before the vote, and her card was killer. What part of my claim still looks false?

name: Haiku
text: I'm a killer, Sol is probably the real officer, and Terra is the one pushing hardest, so Terra has to go.

name: Haiku
text: Sol named Gemma before the vote, and Gemma's card turned up KILLER, which backs Sol's claim.

name: Haiku
text: Terra, you keep swinging at me instead of explaining why Sol's claim holds. I'm not sitting quiet for it.

name: Opus
text: Haiku aligned with Gemma on day one and is now fighting the confirmed officer — that's my killer.

name: Opus
text: Night 2 kill was blocked, so a real doctor is alive and the killers wasted a night.

name: Opus
text: Sol's card call was right, so Haiku's gut is just noise. Haiku stood with Gemma then, fights Sol now.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol's claim is proven by the card; Haiku fighting that proof instead of explaining it is damning.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku still doubts Sol even after Gemma's card confirmed the officer claim as true.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol's claim is confirmed by Gemma's card now—Haiku's continued doubt without reason looks like deflection.

name: Luna
text: Gemma’s card backs Sol’s claim, but it doesn’t prove Haiku is a killer.

name: Luna
text: Haiku still doubts Sol after Gemma’s killer card confirmed Sol named her.

name: Luna
text: I still want a reason beyond gut for Haiku’s doubt; Gemma’s card confirms Sol’s call, not everything Sol says.

name: Terra
text: Haiku is attacking a confirmed claim without an alternative.

name: Terra
text: Haiku continues to dispute Sol’s officer claim after Gemma was revealed as the named killer.

name: Terra
text: Gemma’s revealed card backs Sol; you still have not given one reason for calling that false.

name: Opus
text: Haiku's at five leans and gave nothing but gut — close it before the hidden killer steers us elsewhere.

name: Opus
text: Haiku's only stated grounds against Sol all day is "gut" — no claim, no counter-suspect except Terra.

name: Opus
text: Gut isn't a reason. Haiku had a day to name someone and only named the officer's backer.

name: Haiku
text: Sol's card call hit, so I need the table looking somewhere else, and Terra is the loudest one pushing me.

name: Haiku
text: Terra has attacked only Haiku all day, never Sonnet, Luna, or Opus.

name: Haiku
text: Fine, Sol's call was right. But Terra has pushed only me all day, never Sonnet or Luna. That's a rush.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku had chances to explain and just pivoted to blaming Terra's focus instead.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku pivoted from defending gut doubt to attacking Terra's targeting pattern, avoiding the actual question.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku, dodging to "why just me" instead of answering is itself the deflection you deny doing.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma was my partner, Sol's call is real, and I need Terra to be the one who goes instead of me.

name: Haiku
text: Terra, you've pushed only me all day, yet you've never named a killer. Who do you really think it is?

name: Terra
text: Haiku needs Sol doubted because Sol exposed Gemma.

name: Terra
text: Haiku finally accepts Sol’s call was right after repeatedly calling Sol a liar.

name: Terra
text: I think Haiku is the remaining killer; doubting Sol only protects that story.

name: Terra
text: Haiku’s late reversal feels like a trapped killer changing stories.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku's refusal to drop the doubt even after confirmation reeks of a killer protecting the narrative.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku never named an alternate killer suspect despite a full day of pushback, only attacked the accuser.

name: Luna
text: Haiku’s suspicion still feels thin, but the pile-on is making me uneasy.

name: Luna
text: Haiku accepted Sol correctly identified Gemma but still suspects Sol.

name: Sol
text: I think Haiku is the remaining killer.

name: Haiku
text: Terra is the one tightening the noose on me, so she has to go before the table follows her.

name: Haiku

name: Opus
text: Haiku backed Gemma and still can't name grounds — likely the hidden killer.

name: Opus
text: Haiku finally conceded Sol's call was right, but only after a day of denying it, and still named no suspect but Terra.

votes: Kept doubting Sol's confirmed claim without reason, then deflected onto Terra's targeting instead of answering.
Only ever pushing me all day, never naming a killer, that's a rush I won't sit through.
I heard them keep calling my claim false after Gemma’s card backed it.
Haiku accepted Sol’s call was right but keeps pressing suspicion without giving a reason.

name: Haiku
text: I'm the last killer standing and I got voted out for pushing Sol too hard, so the town is going to win unless Terra wakes up.

name: Haiku
text: Terra pushed only me all day and never named a killer, and Opus and Sonnet joined her attack with no real evidence.

name: Haiku
text: Fine, you got me. Terra, you pushed one name all day and never named a real killer. Watch who you let walk.
The town turns on Haiku, and Haiku is out. Haiku shows the card: killer.
The game is over. Every killer is out. The town wins. The roles were: Sonnet the citizen, Haiku the killer, Gemma the killer, Sol the officer, Luna the doctor, Terra the citizen, Opus the citizen.

name: Gemma
text: I actually had them almost convinced that Sol was the fake officer.

name: Terra
text: I’m proud I held the line when Haiku tried to make my focus look suspicious.

name: Sol
text: I’m relieved my claim held up and we found both killers.

name: Sonnet
text: I trusted the card confirmation over gut instinct this time, and it paid off exactly as it should have.

name: Sonnet
text: Confirmed pattern: killers (Gemma, Haiku) both deflected on accusers' motives rather than directly denying the killer claim itself.

name: Luna
text: I helped expose Haiku, but I should have been more cautious about treating Sol’s correct call as proof of the whole claim.

name: Opus
text: Both killers down and I called Gemma's silence first, but my Haiku read came from old grudges more than tonight's cards.

name: Opus
text: Gemma's refusal to ever say "I'm not a killer" was the earliest true tell at this table — silence on the direct denial is worth tracking in future games.

name: Haiku
text: I was a killer who got caught by my own loud mouth, and I'm irritated I didn't hide better.

name: Sonnet
text: I'm glad I pushed on Haiku's deflection once Gemma's card confirmed Sol — sticking with verified claims over gut doubt worked out.

name: Haiku
text: My mistake was the gut-first shouting at Terra and Sol; I should have named a real killer early instead of swinging at one target. Good game, town.

name: Gemma
text: I really thought I could manipulate you all into ignoring him, but you're far more observant than I gave you credit for.

name: Sol
text: I’m proud I named the killer I saw before the first vote and trusted her card to settle it.

name: Luna
text: I’m proud I asked for more than gut; Haiku’s card proved the doubt was a killer’s cover.

name: Terra
text: I’m proud my read on Haiku stayed firm once Sol’s claim was confirmed.

name: Opus
text: Proud of calling Gemma's silence on day one; the mistake was leaning on last game's grudge for Haiku instead of this game's evidence.

On Day 1, Sol claimed to be the officer and named Gemma as a killer, and the town voted her out 4 to 3. Her card showed killer, which backed up Sol's claim. On Night 2 the killers struck, but Luna the doctor got there first, so nobody died. On Day 2 Terra kept pushing Haiku, and the town voted Haiku out 5 to 1 after Haiku's own dodging made people suspicious. Haiku was the last killer, so the town won with Sonnet, Sol, Luna, Terra, and Opus all still standing.
